Title: Reconcile D0026 LLM-judgment gap with current DispatchPlan caller-context contract

Description:
D0026/Native-First Dispatch Doctrine ghi rõ còn thiếu một lớp quyết định tự động áp rule 1-4, đặc biệt phát hiện "caller đang là soul sống cùng provider hay không" trước khi chọn native vs cli/spawn. Các quyết định sau đó (0033, 0034, DispatchPlan redesign) đã thu hẹp/canonical hóa dispatch nhưng chưa nói rõ gap này được giải quyết, supersede, hay deferred.

Hiện code thực tế dùng một contract khác: caller truyền --has-live-task-access; compileDispatchPlan và decideExecutorDispatchMechanism chỉ áp logic cơ học từ input đó, không tự LLM-judge context. Cần reconcile doctrine với implementation hiện tại để không còn một gap kiến trúc treo ngầm.

Evidence:
- D0026 gap: forgentX/docs/specs/runner.md:1787 nói chưa có lớp tự động áp rule 1-4.
- Current contract: forgentX/docs/how-to/wire-a-skill-through-the-native-vs-cli-spawn-dispatch-decision.md:33 nói --has-live-task-access là self-declaration, không env probe.
- Current mechanism code: forgentX/src/runner/dispatch/mechanism.mjs:14 nhận hasLiveTaskAccess như input.
- DispatchPlan redesign thiếu explicit reconciliation: forgentX/docs/architect/dispatch-control-plane-redesign.md:143.

Scope:
Docs/decision reconciliation first. Touch likely:
- docs/specs/runner.md
- docs/architect/dispatch-control-plane-redesign.md
- docs/how-to/wire-a-skill-through-the-native-vs-cli-spawn-dispatch-decision.md
- optional new docs/history/<task>/CONTEXT.md decision record

Required Decision:
Chọn một trong hai hướng và ghi rõ:
1. Supersede/clarify: D0026's "LLM judgment layer" is now implemented as caller-side judgment plus explicit --has-live-task-access; dispatch core must stay deterministic.
2. Deferred target: The LLM judgment layer is still open, with named future consumer and exact boundary; current --has-live-task-access remains interim.

Acceptance Criteria:
- dispatch-control-plane-redesign.md explicitly mentions the D0026 gap and its current status.
- Docs distinguish caller judgment from dispatch-core mechanism selection.
- No doc implies DispatchPlan auto-detects live soul/provider if it does not.
- No new LLM/subprocess judge is added without a concrete consumer and tests.

Verify:
rg -n "CHƯA có lớp quyết định|has-live-task-access|live Task access|soul sống|Native-First" docs src/runner/dispatch
All hits should consistently state whether this is superseded, current caller contract, or deferred.

payload.title: Title: fgOS submit's dependency-candidate scan misses `delivered` items, letting near-duplicate…
payload.description:
Title: fgOS submit's dependency-candidate scan misses `delivered` items, letting near-duplicate work land

Description:
`/fgOS:submit`'s own step 2 (reused verbatim by `/fgOS:cook`'s own step 1) scans for a duplicate/dependency candidate via `fgos list --json` with no `--all` flag. That default scope excludes `delivered`/`retrospective`/`cleanup`/`done` statuses entirely. An item that has already merged to main but has not yet run through retrospective/cleanup (status `delivered`) is therefore invisible to the exact heuristic meant to catch a duplicate submission.

Live-reproduced this session (tsk-1dd): work item tsk-17m reconciled the D0026/Native-First Dispatch Doctrine narrative gap and merged to `main` via commit 7120a3ed at 14:56 (status `delivered`). ~90 minutes later, tsk-1dd was submitted asking to reconcile the exact same gap. The submit-step's own dependency scan (`fgos list --json`, default scope) ran against a live list dump that did NOT include tsk-17m at all, because it was already `delivered`. The duplicate was only caught later, during discovery-stage research (git log/git show/git merge-base), after tsk-1dd had already gone through submit plus a full discovery pass -- wasting a complete downstream cycle (planning, validating, an out-of-process agy dispatch, executing, approve) to reach the conclusion "already done, nothing to implement."

Evidence:
- plugins/fgOS/skills/submit/SKILL.md step 2's own scan command: `list --json` (no `--all`).
- A live default-scope dump taken during this session (tsk-1dd's own submit step, generated_at 2026-08-26T16:13:31Z) contained zero items with status delivered/retrospective/cleanup/done; its status distribution was {todo:103, doing:13, blocked:6, awaiting-human:5, backlog:1, awaiting-approval:1}.
- tsk-17m's own status at that time: delivered (commit 7120a3ed, 2026-08-26 14:56), confirmed absent from that dump by direct lookup.
- docs/history/tsk-1dd-d0026-gap-duplicate-check/RESEARCH.md -- this session's own root-cause writeup for the tsk-1dd/tsk-17m collision, already merged to main.

Required decision: how to close this gap. Options to consider (not prescribing one):
1. Widen submit's own dependency-candidate scan to `--all` (or specifically include `delivered`/`retrospective`/`cleanup`, excluding only `done`), since a not-yet-fully-closed-out item is still a legitimate duplicate-detection candidate.
2. Leave the scan as-is but document the blind spot plainly in submit's own SKILL.md so a caller knows to widen the search manually for anything that smells like recently-shipped work.
3. Some other mitigation (e.g. a dedicated recency-based check, distinct from the dependency-candidate heuristic).

Scope: likely `plugins/fgOS/skills/submit/SKILL.md` (and wherever its canonical source lives), possibly wherever `fgos list`'s default status-filter set is defined in `src/state`.

Verify: leave to discovery/planning stage to define a real one -- e.g. re-run the dependency scan against a synthetic `delivered` item and confirm it now surfaces as a candidate.
